blocks.text: Oxidation of organic compounds with oxygen is usually combustion: C2H6 + 7/2 O2 gives 2CO2 + 3H2O. Reactions with oxidising agents are also oxidations: ozonolysis is the oxidative cleaving of alkenes with ozone; epoxidation of an alkene is an oxidation using oxidising agents such as molecular oxygen with metal catalysts; and primary alcohols react with acidified K2Cr2O7 to give carboxylic acids, C2H5OH + 2[O] giving CH3COOH + H2O (details in Class XII).

Addition of hydrogen to a carbon-carbon double bond to form an alkane is an organic reduction. Various reducing agents are used in organic synthesis, such as LiAlH4, NaBH4 and Sn with concentrated HCl; for example ethanal with LiAlH4, CH3CHO + 2[H] giving CH3CH2OH. Reduction of nitriles to amines, amides to amines, carboxylic acids to primary alcohols and nitrobenzene to phenylamine are further examples studied in Class XII.
